successors.name: South Africa
successors.text: Natal Province, one of the four founding provinces

ledger.x: 1843: Mpande gives Natal the Buffalo-Tugela country.
4 May 1843: Natal becomes a British colony.
October 1899: the Boers invade northern Natal.
October 1899: Free State commandos join the invasion.
28 February 1900: Ladysmith is relieved, ending the main Free State occupation of northern Natal as well.
January 1903: the Vryheid, Utrecht and Wakkerstroom districts pass to Natal.
31 May 1910: the Colony of Natal becomes Natal Province of the Union of South Africa.

wars.name: Second Boer War (Natal front)
wars.outcome: Boer invasion of northern Natal in October 1899, siege of Ladysmith to 28 February 1900; Treaty of Vereeniging 31 May 1902; the Vryheid and Utrecht districts passed from the Transvaal to Natal in January 1903.

certainty.note: Colonial boundaries (Tugela, Buffalo, the Drakensberg, the Zululand line); the Drakensberg northern limit dates from August 1843, the Zululand boundary vanishes with the 1897 annexation and the Transvaal line moves in January 1903.
